evidence_packet.title: Teen who went into care at 10 calls system 'fundamentally flawed'
evidence_packet.lead: Young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population
evidence_packet.summary: Young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Teen who went into care at 10 calls system 'fundamentally flawed' - BBC News Image caption, Hayden said he would like to see significant changes in the care system By Lauren Hirst North West Published 25 minutes ago A teenager who went into care when he was 10 has described how he struggled to navigate the system and seek help. Hayden, now aged 17, lived in a children's home until he was 16 before moving into a semi-independent home. After feeling unsafe there he ended up sofa-surfing. "There is an incredible amount of individuals working so hard to improve the lives of young people but the system is fundamentally flawed," said Hayden, who got in touch with the BBC via Your Voice to share his experience. A new government-commissioned report found that young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population . The report noted the potentially catastrophic consequences for those who are often left alone "with no safety net". People leaving care in England at 18 often lose "significant levers of support", the report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed. "You kind of are navigating it by yourself and just hoping you've said the right things and put the right things forward to make things happen," said Hayden, who grew up in Middleton, Greater Manchester, before being placed in care in a different local authority area. "We are not the undeserving poor of the Victorian era. "People deserve compassion because they have been through so much." 'It wasn't easy' Hayden, who turns 18 next month, is currently living in a semi-independent placement in Oldham while studying at a sixth-form college. title: How did student midwife Success Eduan win European athletics gold?

evidence_packet.summary: Success Eduan balanced studying for her three-year midwife degree with her training as an elite athlete
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Getting to the top in any sport involves not only talent but also huge dedication and personal sacrifice Something the aptly named Success Eduan knows all about After reaching the individual 200m final at the recent European Championships in Birmingham, the 21-year-old athlete from Manchester won gold in the women's 4x100m relay Unknown to many, though, Eduan combined her gruelling training regime with completing a three-year degree in midwifery "It took a lot of grit, a lot of determination," the sprinter told BBC North West "There [were] times where I've not been able to fully train, just because mentally I'm exhausted from night shifts or from exams and things like that."

title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross
evidence_packet.lead: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.summary: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans

evidence_packet.title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans
evidence_packet.lead: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
evidence_packet.summary: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043 Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039 The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001

evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:30, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The Tootal buildings in Manchester An interim top boss has been chosen to run Greater Manchester alongside mayor Bev Craig after the previous chief executive was poached to work in Number 10 North Andrew Lightfoot’s name was put forward on Friday (August 30) to step up from his job as deputy to formally become interim group chief executive at the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which also includes Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service The post comes with a wage of £245,000 and serves as the GMCA’s head of paid service - its most senior officer - as well as returning officer and director general of Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) The recommendation needs to be approved on September 25 while the search for a permanent chief begins Former GMCA boss Caroline Simpson stepped down in July to join Andy Burnham's team at Heron House in the Prime Minister’s Manchester office, which opened an ‘immediate gap’ to be plugged at the Combined Authority

title: 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it'

evidence_packet.title: 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it'
evidence_packet.lead: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this.
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Taco Bell horror as boy stabbed in toilets after '25 youths ran in with knives' before diners desperately saved victim's life Police cordoned off Taco Bell in Rochdale after the attack with a major investigation underway News Amy Walker Court A 13-year-old boy has been left with serious injuries after being stabbed in Taco Bell in Rochdale . Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , David Lane told of the 'horrific moment' and how his actions helped save the boy "We sat down and ordered our food at around 5.50pm, then a load of kids came in and started fighting," he said. "I got up and went to one of the crew members at Taco Bell and asked them to kick them out because my family were there "I told them to lock the door, and they never did. About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Traffic and travel LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 9 hours ago Man dies after train crashes into van in major incident at Burscough with lines shut The incident appears to have taken place near Martin Lane in Burscough with trains between Wigan and Southport Images shared online show a Northern train that has stopped next to green fields. Several ambulances and a fire engine could be seen at the scene in the Burscough area Tragically, in a statement tonight, British Transport Police have said a man who was in the van has died. Posting on X, Northern said: "Due to the emergency services dealing with an incident Wigan Wallgate - Southport all lines are blocked. Restrictions will be reinstated once the disruption ends." BTP added: "The incident is not being treated as suspicious. Enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'Growing up with Wigan bogeyman inspired my own love of horror' Author David Barnett's childhood growing up in Ince, Wigan, inspired his own horror stories Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 16:32, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 16:41, 29 Aug 202 As horror aficionados know, classic folk horror is often set in the isolated countryside - where the natural landscape, archaic traditions and rituals and the dark power of nature lend themselves to the genre But for writer David Barnett, his folk horror is born from the red-brick terraces and slagheaps of Wigan. Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. But the unifying feature was where the name came from. Its clogs were red because they were dripping with blood, usually from kicking someone to death

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Two months of raging wildfires near Greater Manchester, finally over but not forgotten The M.E.N takes a look back at the devastating fires at Dovestone and Swineshaw, Tintwistle and Saddleworth this summer View 11 Images A hazy view of Manchest News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 15:50, 29 Aug 2026 The huge raging wildfires that broke out near Greater Manchester this summer are finally extinguished Hundreds of firefighters battled blazes at Dovestone and Swineshaw, Tintwistle and Saddleworth with two major incidents declared in July. As the blazes took hold of the vast moorland areas, parts of Greater Manchester, including in some areas miles away, were left covered in smok The wildfires smouldered amid several heatwaves, with very little respite from hot and dry weather. Miles of scorched moorland and devastated wildlife has been left behind In the wake of the wildfires, and the hundreds that have broken out across the country this summer, concerns have been raised over tougher consequences for those who start them with most beginning 'due to human activities'. Below we take a look back at the response and impact of During one of the first heatwaves of the year on June 24, a wildfire started burning on Tintwistle Moor. The vast, scenic moorland sits above Woodhead Road near Glossop, on the border of Tameside and Derbyshire

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:30, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The Tootal buildings in Manchester An interim top boss has been chosen to run Greater Manchester alongside mayor Bev Craig after the previous chief executive was poached to work in Number 10 North Andrew Lightfoot’s name was put forward on Friday (August 30) to step up from his job as deputy to formally become interim group chief executive at the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which also includes Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service The post comes with a wage of £245,000 and serves as the GMCA’s head of paid service - its most senior officer - as well as returning officer and director general of Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) The recommendation needs to be approved on September 25 while the search for a permanent chief begins Former GMCA boss Caroline Simpson stepped down in July to join Andy Burnham's team at Heron House in the Prime Minister’s Manchester office, which opened an ‘immediate gap’ to be plugged at the Combined Authority

title: 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it'

evidence_packet.title: 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it'
evidence_packet.lead: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this.
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale Taco Bell horror as boy stabbed in toilets after '25 youths ran in with knives' before diners desperately saved victim's life Police cordoned off Taco Bell in Rochdale after the attack with a major investigation underway News Amy Walker Court A 13-year-old boy has been l
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Taco Bell horror as boy stabbed in toilets after '25 youths ran in with knives' before diners desperately saved victim's life Police cordoned off Taco Bell in Rochdale after the attack with a major investigation underway News Amy Walker Court A 13-year-old boy has been left with serious injuries after being stabbed in Taco Bell in Rochdale . Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , David Lane told of the 'horrific moment' and how his actions helped save the boy "We sat down and ordered our food at around 5.50pm, then a load of kids came in and started fighting," he said. "I got up and went to one of the crew members at Taco Bell and asked them to kick them out because my family were there "I told them to lock the door, and they never did. About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

evidence_packet.summary: Traffic and travel LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 9 hours ago Man dies after train crashes into van in major incident at Burscough with lines shut The incident appears to have taken place near Martin Lane in Burscough with trains between Wigan and Southport Images shared online show a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Traffic and travel LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 9 hours ago Man dies after train crashes into van in major incident at Burscough with lines shut The incident appears to have taken place near Martin Lane in Burscough with trains between Wigan and Southport Images shared online show a Northern train that has stopped next to green fields. Several ambulances and a fire engine could be seen at the scene in the Burscough area Tragically, in a statement tonight, British Transport Police have said a man who was in the van has died. Two train passengers were injured in the crash, police added All services on the main line remain cancelled tonight. Posting on X, Northern said: "Due to the emergency services dealing with an incident Wigan Wallgate - Southport all lines are blocked. Please note that other train operators may also be affected by disruption – please check "Northern train ticket restrictions have been lifted in the affected areas, including Advance and Peak restrictions, during this disruption. Restrictions will be reinstated once the disruption ends." BTP added: "The incident is not being treated as suspicious. Enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'Growing up with Wigan bogeyman inspired my own love of horror' Author David Barnett's childhood growing up in Ince, Wigan, inspired his own horror stories Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 16:32, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 16:41, 29 Aug 202 As horror aficionados know, classic folk horror is often set in the isolated countryside - where the natural landscape, archaic traditions and rituals and the dark power of nature lend themselves to the genre But for writer David Barnett, his folk horror is born from the red-brick terraces and slagheaps of Wigan. Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. But the unifying feature was where the name came from. Its clogs were red because they were dripping with blood, usually from kicking someone to death

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Man fights for life following Salford flats balcony plunge horror as police question attempted murder suspect CSI were pictured working on a balcony on the top floor View 4 Images Scenes of crime investigators pictured on a top-floor balcony ( News Paul Britton Reporter and Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 12:19, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 14:27, 29 Aug 2026 A man has been arrested on suspicion of the attempted murder of a man who fell from a balcony at a block of flats The suspect, aged in his 20s, was in custody for questioning on Saturday (August 29) as the man who fell, also believed to be in his 20s, was fighting for his life in hospital Police said he was taken to hospital from the scene in Langworthy, Salford , with 'life-threatening injuries' and remained there in a 'critical condition' on Saturday afternoon. Police chiefs said it is believed to be an 'isolated incident' with no wider risk to the public Reports from residents living nearby the scene - a block of flats on Southern Street, off Liverpool Street - said members of the public rushed to help the man who fell and performed CPR on him. It's also claimed the aftermath of the horror was filmed and streamed on TikTok How far the man fell hasn't been confirmed, but specialist scenes of crime investigators were pictured inside the flats on Saturday morning working on a top-floor balcony

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Pride When the rain will stop today in Manchester as 2026 Pride takes place in city centre Met Office forecasts show that the rain is set to persist throughout Saturday afternoon Comments News Miranda Pell Search and Discover Writer 13:08, August Bank Holiday weekend has gotten off to a very wet start, with festivals and other major events taking place all over the UK It comes after the UK has seen an uncharacteristically dry and hot summer, with record-breaking heatwaves and droughts. So for some, this rain is welcome. But for others, it could do with stopping until the end of the long bank holiday weekend Manchester Village Pride 2026 is taking place in the city centre today, after celebrations got underway on Friday, August 28. The parade is taking place from 12pm and then the party will continue in the village until the late hours This year's LGBTQ+ event was created following the voluntary liqudation of the company behind Manchester Pride last year. As a result, a new Community Interest Company (CIC) was founded, with a new focus on the community and with the support of the many venues and bars that make Reiterating the core message behind the new-look event, this year's Parade will take on the theme of 'No Place Like Home'. Not only serving as a nod to queer classic The Wizard of Oz, it will also hone in on the special meaning of home and belonging within a chosen family

Unbeknown to him, the flashy criminal Hanson had been under surveillance Cops from GMP's Serious and Organised Crime Group watched as he visited a drugs stash house in Radcliffe, Bury, and drove around Radcliffe, Whitefield and Greenmount They saw him make street deals with users - then made their move just after 3pm on May 22, at the junction of Bury New Road and Chestnut Avenue in Whitefield. Hanson, 20, who spent thousands on designer clothes, 'attempted to evade arrest', Greater Manchester Police said this wee The officers involved in what became a firearms operation attempted to stop the Cupra, but the force said Hanson failed to comply and 'attempted to evade capture' In turn, officers discharged a single shot, striking him in the elbow. A sentencing hearing in court was told one of the attending armed officers 'felt compelled to discharge his firearm'

evidence_packet.summary: The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming g
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park From humble beginnings performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage, the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005 Sitting upstairs in the pub, Fray smiled at the 3ft (0.9m) stage and single spotlight on the ceiling while recalling the night he spent there more than two decades ago "It's unusual to be in here and it's exactly the same," he said. "It is very small."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

The Everton manager In contrast to the Everton chief executive, Angus Kinnear, who recently claimed the club were planning to challenge for Europe this season, Moyes insisted the squad needs “a lot of work” before it can achieve that target City have yet to bid for Ndiaye, who has three years remaining on his Everton contract but declined several offers of an extension last season as they did not include a release clause for a Champions League club. “I think it would be very difficult to get it reinvested if anythin On Ndiaye, he added: “I’m certainly not encouraging a bid. I’m not encouraging that in a million years. I don’t know if it would be too tight for time. Deals and contracts are taking much longer now. There seems to be a lot more involved.” Everton remain interested in City’s Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but a right-back and centre-forward are more of a priority. Moyes added: “I’m saying there’s not much time but I’ll still try to see what we can do. Its approach is rooted in tradition but interpreted through a contemporary lens – cr At the heart of Coco Tang is a belief that Vietnamese hospitality extends far beyond food, with the experience beginning with the first coffee of the day and continuing through to the final cocktail of the night. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
